findings.title: @cfunc UDAF callbacks have no exception guard: a raise inside an impl leaks the borrowed structref incref and returns a silent wrong default to DuckDB
findings.description: Every DuckDB callback is a thin @cfunc wrapper forwarding to a module-level @njit impl, and none of the impls wrap their body in try/except (init irr.py:114-126, update :129-167, combine :170-190, finalize :193-211, destroy :214-225). Per the documented numba @cfunc behavior (user reference 'numba @cfunc swallows exceptions': returns the zero default + does NOT unwind to C, and leaks any NRT refs held across the raising call), an exception unwinding out of an impl through the @cfunc boundary is swallowed: DuckDB sees a normal return (uint64 0 for state_size, void otherwise) and proceeds. The concrete leak path: in update/combine/finalize the impl holds a live borrowed structref `s` from borrow_structref (numbox/utils/meminfo.py:131-140), which does `_incref_meminfo(p)` (+1) and is balanced ONLY by the normal scope-exit decref of the local. update calls vector_push (irr.py:157-158) and combine calls vector_extend (irr.py:180-181); both (numbox/core/vector/vector.py:121-127, :131-141) conditionally reallocate via numpy.empty, an NRT allocation that can raise MemoryError. If that raise (or any OOB with NUMBA_BOUNDSCHECK=1, or a bad/zero state pointer turned into an exception) fires while `s` is borrowed, the scope-exit decref is skipped -> the group's MemInfo (and its nested vectors) leak, and because the @cfunc swallows the exception DuckDB keeps the half-mutated/garbage state and emits a silently wrong aggregate value with no SQL-level error. _irr_state_size_cb returning 0 on a (hypothetical) raise would be worse still, causing DuckDB to allocate 0-byte state slots that init then overwrites with an 8-byte pointer (heap overflow), though state_size here is a constant and cannot raise.
findings.impact: On any error condition (allocation failure during a vector grow, malformed chunk, OOB read) the aggregate leaks one MemInfo per affected group and returns a silently incorrect result to SQL instead of surfacing an error. The exact failure class the numbox cfunc reference warns about.
findings.recommendation: Wrap each impl body in a bare try/except (the numbox reference notes a bare try/except cures both the swallow and the NRT leak). At minimum guard update/combine/finalize, releasing/decrefing the borrowed state on the error path and signalling failure (e.g. duckdb_*_set_error or writing NaN). Do not use try/finally (reraises on numba 0.65.1 per the same reference).

findings.title: borrow_structref net-zero refcount across update/combine/finalize is upheld by different (inlining-dependent) mechanisms per stage; currently balanced only by the example's own NRT self-check
findings.description: The borrow contract requires the +1 incref inside borrow_structref (numbox/utils/meminfo.py:139, separate @njit whose StructRef return type disables removerefctpass so the incref provably survives) to be cancelled by the borrowed local's scope-exit decref in the calling impl. But the impls have no-NRT signatures (void(intp,...)), so their scope-exit decref is a strip candidate for removerefctpass. The decref only survives if either (a) borrow_structref is inlined into the impl before the pass runs, or (b) some non-allowlisted NRT alloc symbol is present in the impl. update/combine satisfy (b) incidentally because vector_push/vector_extend can realloc (numbox vector.py:122-123,:137); finalize (irr.py:193-211) does NO allocation, so it relies entirely on (a). numbox's bridge helpers are plain @njit with no forced inline=, so the finalize case depends on LLVM inlining + pass ordering rather than anything guaranteed. The happy-path balance is real on the tested numba version (the example's main() NRT self-check at irr.py:372-377 sys.exit(1)s on any alloc/free mismatch and the pattern is merged upstream), but a numba upgrade that changes inlining/pass ordering, or an innocuous edit removing the vector op from update/combine, would flip a borrow into a +1-per-row leak (or, mirror-image, an early free) with no compile-time signal.
findings.impact: Latent: a future numba version or a small refactor could silently introduce a per-group/per-row MemInfo leak (or premature free -> use-after-free) in the UDAF state path, undetected except by the runtime NRT self-check.
findings.recommendation: Keep the main() NRT alloc/free self-check (irr.py:372-377) as a CI assertion, and ideally force-inline the numbox bridge helpers (inline='always') or store both meminfo_p and data_p and incref via the @intrinsic _incref_meminfo (the array-state variant the authors already use in test/ for exactly this reason) so the refcount balance no longer depends on optimizer inlining.

notes: Sound aspects verified (no defect): (1) Happy-path refcount IS balanced. init allocates the structref + two vectors (refct 1 each) and export_meminfo (numbox meminfo.py:143-152) adds the slot's +1; _irr_init_impl contains NRT_MemInfo_alloc (constructing Float64Vector/IRRState) which disables removerefctpass, so the creation incref and scope-exit decref both survive -> slot owns exactly +1 (irr.py:114-126). destroy does exactly one release_meminfo per group via the direct NRT_MemInfo_release call (numbox meminfo.py:90-111), which survives the pass by design (irr.py:214-225). Each state gets exactly one init (+1) and one destroy (-1); combine does not release its operands; DuckDB destroys every state. (2) DuckDB aggregate ABI is handled correctly: init receives a single state buffer; update/combine/finalize/destroy receive a void** array of state pointers, and irr.py reads the outer array then a 1-element inner carray over each 8-byte slot (irr.py:144/155, 172-177, 196-200, 216-219) -> no out-of-bounds. state_size==8 matches sizeof(intp). (3) _cast_int_to_void_p and _deref_structref_raw_ptr/borrow_structref are used within contract: every pointer fed to _cast_int_to_void_p is intp; borrow_structref receives (TypeRef irr_state_type, intp slot[0]) so _require_intp (numbox meminfo.py:67-74) passes; no truncating inttoptr. (4) @cfunc objects and ducklib CompileResultWAP wrappers are module-level globals, so the JIT code backing the registered C function pointers stays mapped for process lifetime (no dangling callback). One latent coupling worth a guard: state_size==8 is hardcoded and silently assumes the slot holds exactly one intp; a future variant storing both meminfo_p and data_p (as the test array-state bridge does) must bump it to 16 or init's slot[1] store overflows the 8-byte buffer. pybridge.extract_connection_ptr's get_unicode_data_p('SELECT 1') aliases a live numba string payload (numbox RISK-4) but is safe here because the literal lives in co_consts and is consumed immediately; pybridge lifetime/from_address concerns are owned by unit PBR-MEM. The borrow net-zero fragility could not be empirically measured (no execution permitted); MEM-2 is rated low because the shipped NRT self-check and the upstream merge indicate it currently balances.
